notes: Standard deduction: the booklet prints no standard deduction (the words do not appear in the booklet or the Schedule M). West Virginia's starting point is federal AGI, and federal deductions are not allowed: 'the only itemized deductions allowed to be claimed from the federal income tax return are gambling losses' (PDF page 21 section 'Itemized Deductions'; Schedule M line 46). The Tax Division page calls the 8,000 senior citizen modification 'similar in operation to the federal standard deduction'; it is a relief here (wv_senior_citizen_deduction), for people 65 or older or disabled only.

Brackets: Rate Schedule I (PDF page 37) names Single, Head of household, Married filing joint and Widow[er] with dependent child, so head_of_household and qualifying_surviving_spouse have no schedule of their own. Rate Schedule II is for married filing separately.

Brackets: filers under Rate Schedule I with taxable income under 100,000 use the Tax Table (PDF pages 38 onward). Every one of its 1,702 rows checked equals Rate Schedule I at the row's midpoint, rounded to the whole dollar. The schedule's printed 'tax plus rate' amounts (222.00, 666.00, 1,165.50, 2,053.50; 111.00, 333, 582.75, 1,026.75) are the sums of the lower bands, so no band has a base.

Governments of other states: 'New York' does not appear in the booklet, and no line names another state's government pension. Lines 31 and 33(a) name West Virginia systems only and line 33(b) names Federal Retirement. Treatment of public_pension_other_state: not found in the booklet. Such a pension stays in federal AGI and is taxed, and only the age 65 or disability deduction can reach it, because that deduction takes any income.

Private pensions, IRA and employer-plan distributions and annuities: not found as a subtraction in the booklet. They stay in federal AGI; the PDF page 30 example lists 'IRA Distributions' in total income and subtracts them nowhere but through the 8,000 senior deduction. The only private-pension line is the PBGC Modification (line 45). Roth conversions: the word Roth does not appear in the booklet (not found in the booklet). Line 54 adds back qualifying 402(e) lump sums taxed on federal Form 4972.

Social Security: treatment is relief. Line 34 subtracts benefits included in federal AGI, 100% at or under the AGI limit and for 2025 65% above it. The AGI limit is tested on the return (a joint return's federal AGI against 100,000). The form's line 34 box names only single, married separate and married joint; the instructions (PDF pages 17 and 28) add head of household and widow(er) at 50,000.

Scheduled change (for tax years after 2025): the Tax Division page says the share above the AGI limit was 35% for 2024 and 65% for 2025 and 'In Tax Year 2026, it will become a 100% decreasing modification', so from 2026 taxable Social Security is subtracted in full at any income. The page adds that many people will see the benefit only in 2026, because line 34 uses up the 8,000 senior deduction.

PDF page 29 line 40 says Social Security benefits 'that are taxable on your federal return are also taxable to West Virginia'. That sentence is about what not to enter on the railroad line, and it does not override line 34.

Line numbers: the Schedule M instructions keep older numbers from line 47 on, two higher than the 2025 form (box (c) says lines 35 through 48 where the form and the example say 35 to 46; the example's table is numbered 49; 'LINE 49 Add lines 29 through 50' is the form's 'Add lines 29 through 48'). This record uses the form's numbers.
Line 47 disability: PDF page 29 says 'taxpayers under age 65', PDF page 23 says 'regardless of age'. A person 65 or older qualifies as a senior anyway, so no max_age is set.

Line 47 senior and disability entries are one line with one 8,000 for each person: a person who qualifies both ways gets one deduction. Each spouse is tested separately, so one spouse may claim as a senior and the other as disabled.

Other Schedule M subtractions, not retirement relief and not recorded: S corporation bank assets (35), state and local tax refunds (38), college savings contributions (39), long-term care insurance premiums (41), IRC 1341 repayments (42), ABLE (43), Jumpstart deposits (44), gambling losses (46). Income on lines 35 to 46 is left out of line 47 column (c).

Property tax credits (Senior Citizens Tax Credit, Homestead Excess Property Tax Credit, Disabled Veterans Real Property Tax Credit, Property Tax Adjustment Credits) are credits for property tax paid, not relief on income, and are not recorded. The credit for income tax paid to another state is not recorded.
Capital gains: the booklet prints no separate rate or deduction; capital_gains is empty. Surtaxes and recapture: none printed.
Indexing: the booklet says nothing about inflation adjustment ('inflation', 'indexed' and 'adjusted annually' do not appear). Figures are not_stated.

reliefs.cap_rule: Schedule M line 47, for each person: column (c) is that person's income not reported on lines 35 through 46, not to exceed 8000; column (d) is the sum of that person's lines 29 through 34; the deduction is (c) minus (d), and zero if (d) is larger. So lines 29 through 34 and line 47 together come to the higher of the sum of lines 29 through 34 or column (c). Income on lines 29 through 34 stays in column (c): in the PDF page 30 example a person with 13,000 of income, 7,500 of it on lines 29 and 31, enters 8000 in (c), 7500 in (d) and takes 500. Tax Division page: 'You receive the higher of the $8,000 modification or the sum of various itemized decreasing modifications'. Line 47 and the surviving spouse deduction (line 48) share the 8000. Joint income is divided between spouses by percentage of ownership.
